properties.name: Middle Mosel (Mittelmosel / Bernkastel)
properties.category: The world benchmark for slate-driven, featherweight, high-acid Riesling: crystalline lime, white peach, green apple, wet slate, and razor-sharp mineral tension (Wehlener Sonnenuhr, Berncasteler Doctor, Ürziger Würzgarten, Erdener Prälat).
properties.description: The historic heart of the Mosel Valley stretching from Zell to Trier, home to the most famous Riesling vineyards on Earth including Wehlener Sonnenuhr, Berncasteler Doctor, and Erdener Prälat.
properties.source: Bundesamt für Kartographie und Geodäsie (BKG) VG250

properties.name: Saar & Ruwer Tributary Valleys
properties.category: Laser-focused, electric Riesling of celestial lightness and unmatched aging potential (Egon Müller Scharzhofberg, Peter Lauer Ayler Kupp, Karthäuserhofberg).
properties.description: The colder tributary valleys south and east of Trier, renowned for producing the most aristocratic, long-lived, and expensive sweet and dry Rieslings in the world.
properties.source: Bundesamt für Kartographie und Geodäsie (BKG) VG250

properties.name: Rheingau & Central Rhine
properties.category: Aristocratic, powerful dry Riesling (Grosses Gewächs) and historic botrytis dessert wines; world-renowned Spätburgunder in the red slate village of Assmannshausen.
properties.description: The historical epicenter of noble German viticulture where Spätlese (late harvest) was discovered at Schloss Johannisberg in 1775.
properties.source: Bundesamt für Kartographie und Geodäsie (BKG) VG250

properties.name: Nahe & Pfalz (Mittelhaardt)
properties.category: Dry Grosses Gewächs Riesling summits (Dönnhoff Hermannshöhle, Keller G-Max / Hubacker, Bürklin-Wolf Kirchenstück) combining power, smoky minerality, and racy acid.
properties.description: Dynamic southern regions leading Germany's dry wine revolution, home to legendary estates like Weingut Dönnhoff and Weingut Keller.
properties.source: Bundesamt für Kartographie und Geodäsie (BKG) VG250
